headline: Daily research brief — Wednesday, October 7

items.title: TSLA's Oct 21 earnings is the week's watchlist binary; options do not look cheap into it
items.detail: Confirmed on the live Nasdaq calendar today - this corrects the Oct 28 date in the 10/05-10/06 files. Options imply +/-8.2% via the Oct-23 ATM straddle vs a 6.0% mean-absolute reaction over the last four prints, and the July print's -14.5% reaction shows the tail skew. The term structure shows the classic hump: 30DTE IV 43.6% vs front weekly 30.9%. Selling premium into the hump is short gamma into a scheduled binary - off-limits.

items.title: The distillate deficit is the real energy tight spot
items.detail: EIA's weekly released on schedule today at 10:30 AM ET: crude drew 3.2M bbl to 424.1M (1% above the 5-yr avg), but distillates are unchanged at 12% below the 5-yr average into heating season, and diesel is near record highs. The direct offset is the G7's 100M-bbl emergency release, which includes diesel. The call changes on a distillate build next week or confirmed G7 diesel hitting the market.

items.title: 10Y at 5.27%, up 55bp in two months; duration exposure keeps long-dated growth premium expensive
items.detail: The whole-curve move is a parallel bear repricing - 2s10s is flat at 48bp, and SOFR-EFFR at 2bp shows funding is calm. QQQ, NVDA, TSLA, MSFT and AAPL carry the most duration exposure, so long-dated growth-call premium should be treated as expensive until the 10Y confirms a top back under ~5.00%. A +-15bp weekly move in the 2s10s slope would signal a regime shift to price into vol structure.

items.title: Brent-WTI at $11.95 is historically wide; the geopolitical premium is all in seaborne Brent
items.detail: WTI at $89.14 in ~1%/mo backwardation while ME exports exceeded pre-war levels on 4 of the last 7 Sept days and Aramco cut Asia OSPs by $3 - the physical market is less tight than Brent's $100+ handle implies. WTI spec length is washed out near the 10th percentile on COT, so a genuine bullish catalyst could re-leverage fast. VIX 15.08: premium is siloed in energy with no equity-vol spillover.

desks.Futures: EIA released on schedule: crude -3.2M bbl to 424.1M; distillates flat at 12% below the 5-yr avg into heating season; Brent-WTI $11.95 wide. Nat gas storage Thu 10:30 AM ET (+79 Bcf expected, 8th straight surplus-shrink if met); WASDE Fri 12:00 PM ET pricing a record soy crop.
desks.Parity: Quiet - no put-call/box-parity violations or index-methodology changes material to the watchlist since the 10/06 run; the closest reference shows VIX-futures put-call parity holding within ~0.16.
desks.Premium: Nothing above 55%ile IV-rank. NVDA's 0%ile is the cheapest in ~2.4 years but offers no seller's edge (modestly rich vs realized, clean window). MSFT's 55%ile board-high rank is event-driven (11/4 earnings in window), not a sell signal. QQQ/AAPL/MSFT/TSLA verdicts are window-contingent - avoid selling the humps.
